# Testing on both engines

Every store and core test runs on SQLite, and on Postgres as well when `DARKORY_TEST_POSTGRES_URL` is set ([plan invariant 3](plan.md#invariants)). Tests always run with the race detector.

## Running

```sh
make test       # every test, SQLite only; Postgres tests skip
make test-pg    # every test on SQLite and Postgres
make check      # generated code up to date, go vet, then both of the above
DARKORY_TEST_S3=1 DARKORY_TEST_SMTP=1 make test   # also MinIO and Mailpit in Docker
make web-check  # the web app: typecheck, eslint, vitest (needs node; run `npm ci` in web/ first)
make e2e        # the real binary end to end, the bots and the soak, on SQLite (about 3 minutes)
make e2e-pg     # the same on Postgres, plus two server processes on one database (about 6 minutes)
cd web && npm run e2e   # build the web app and the binary, then drive a real server in Chromium (needs node and go; `npx playwright install chromium` once)
```

The end-to-end suite in `e2e/` runs only with `DARKORY_E2E=1`, so `make check` skips it. It builds `darkory` once into a temporary directory, runs `darkory init` and `darkory serve` processes on free ports, and drives them through the CLI, `darkory mcp` over stdio and, for the soak, the generated client; it imports nothing under `internal/`. With `DARKORY_E2E_POSTGRES_URL` set (as `make e2e-pg` does) each test creates its own `dk_e2e_<random>` database and drops it. `DARKORY_E2E_SOAK=5m` makes the soak longer, `DARKORY_E2E_SOAK_TASKS=3000` heavier, and `DARKORY_E2E_RACE=1` builds the binary with the race detector, whose reports fail the run through the server log check.

`make test-pg` sets `DARKORY_TEST_POSTGRES_URL=postgres://dk@localhost:54329/postgres?sslmode=disable`. Point it elsewhere with `make test-pg TEST_POSTGRES_URL=…`, or set the variable yourself for a single package:

```sh
DARKORY_TEST_POSTGRES_URL='postgres://dk@localhost:54329/postgres?sslmode=disable' go test -race ./internal/store/...
```

## Bots

`tools/bots/bot` is a library of bots: agent Members that work an Install as an agent such as Claude Code does — `next`, a Heartbeat in the background, a Note, Evidence, a question, then `advance` along one of the outcomes out of the Task's Step — through the generated client, and, for `stuck`, through the real binary; and human personas that act as people in the web app would, each with a token of their own. Like `e2e/`, it imports nothing under `internal/`. The bots work a **preset**: a Go value (`bot.Preset`) holding the Projects with their defaults, the Skills, one Workflow by names (`bot.WorkflowSpec`: Steps with the Skill each carries, none for a hold, and the Connectors out of each in the order offered) that Setup gives every Project of the preset, the Workspaces (each made as a throwaway git repository), the agents, the personas, the Task templates the owner files and the plans filed under them. A template is filed with Break down (the planner files its Subtasks), alone (one Task worked from its one Item's Step), or as a Parent whose Items are filed as its Subtasks at once. An **Item** is one Subtask of a plan: title, one-line description, the Step it is worked at first, filed ahead into the hold or not, the Items it is blocked by, its Workspaces, the question its worker raises (at which Step, and at whom), the outcome to advance along, the workpaper its worker appends to (one line per Step), and what review sends back along "needs changes" with the fix that answers it. `bot.Setup` makes a preset idempotently by name; `e2e/bots_test.go` (`TestBots`, the software preset) and `e2e/bots_accounting_test.go` (`TestBotsAccounting`), both part of `make e2e` and `make e2e-pg`, run the bots at the `fast` pace as scenario tests; `tools/bots` runs them at the `human` pace as a live load, so the web app can be watched and screenshotted with work going on.

How every worker ends its part (`agent.work`): an Item that names a hand-back is sent back along "needs changes" the first time it is reviewed, and the worker at the Step it lands on appends the fix; otherwise an agent records an Observation (didn't work when it had to ask) and advances along the Item's outcome, else the first outcome of the Step — the way work goes on in the presets' Workflows — while a person completes a Task whose Step has one way out, into Done, and advances anywhere else. A Task at no Step (a question) completes as it is.

### The software preset

Projects `WEB` Web and `OPS` Ops, both on `bot.SoftwareWorkflow`; Skills `build`, `build-acme` (company, on build), `review`, `qa`, `docs`, `triage`, `deploy` and the built-ins; no Workspace. Each kind of work has a Step of its own, since a Task's Skill is its Step's:

| Step | Skill | Outcomes |
|---|---|---|
| Backlog | — (a hold) | — (a person moves a Task on) |
| Plan | breakdown | `done` → Done |
| Build | build-acme | `pass` → Review |
| Docs | docs | `done` → Done |
| QA | qa | `done` → Done |
| Review | review | `pass` → Done · `needs changes` → Build |
| Triage | triage | `done` → Done |
| Deploy | deploy | `done` → Done |
| Retro | retro | `propose` → Skill review · `done` → Done |
| Skill review | skill-review | `publish` → Done · `needs changes` → Retro |

The owner's templates are filed in `WEB` with Break down; the planner files `DefaultPlan` under each: the API and the screen at Build (the screen's description carries `Question for <member>: …`, which any Task filed by hand may carry too), QA at QA blocked by both builds, and a help page, a demo and a polish filed ahead into Backlog. The chores "Rotate the logs" (Triage) and "Deploy to staging" (Deploy) are filed alone in `OPS`.

| Who | Skills | What it does | What it proves |
|---|---|---|---|
| `planner` | breakdown | Takes Breakdowns through `next` and files the Parent's Subtasks with `parent`: the builds at Build; QA into Backlog, blocked by both builds, then moved to QA; the help page, the demo and the polish into Backlog. Advances the Breakdown into Done with a Note. | Filing into a hold and Blocking before anything is takeable. |
| `builder-1`, `builder-2` | build, build-acme, qa | `next` with a model label, Heartbeats in the background, a Note, a small Evidence file. A question in the description is filed aimed at its Member, blocking the Task, and the builder waits holding its Claim (releasing it after `Patience`). Records an Observation, didn't work when it had to ask, and advances along `pass` to Review, or `done` at QA. | Questions, `advance` along an outcome, Observations. |
| `reviewer` | review, skill-review | Advances a review into Done along `pass`; advances a Retrospective at Skill review along `publish`, publishing every pending proposal, and says so when Darkory sends it back to Retro because another version was published since. | Publishing a Skill version, the stale base. |
| `retro` | retro | Reads the Observations on the Parent and its Subtasks, proposes the next version of the company Skill that didn't work (`build-acme`), and advances along `propose` to Skill review; with nothing to change, along `done`. | The Retrospective's proposal. |
| `lapser` | triage | Claims with a 2 s timeout (20 s at the human pace) and never heartbeats. Once in the test; every minute live. | The lapse recorded with no actor; the Task waiting at its Step again. |
| `stuck` | deploy | `darkory next`, then `darkory heartbeat run` keeping the Claim and `darkory heartbeat <task>` checking it until someone takes the Task back, when that command exits 3. | Take-back through the CLI; `heartbeat run` keeps the Session's other Claims (decisions.md). |
| `prober` | docs | A builder that asks `next` without waiting. | `next` offers nothing waiting in the hold until a person moves it. |
| `kai` (persona) | — | Owns the Parents; every round completes those whose Subtasks have all ended and moves one unblocked Task waiting in Backlog, whose Parent's Breakdown has ended, to the Step its Item names (else the Workflow's first work Step); the agents report to him. | The Owner's Complete, the move out of a hold. |
| `mai` (persona) | — | Answers the questions aimed at her: Claim, a Note with the answer, Complete. | A question ends and its Task unblocks. |

`TestBots` runs on an Install `init` seeded with its roster (Setup keeps `planner`, `reviewer` and `retro`, which `init` made), sets the Organisation up with the bots' own `bot.Setup`, twice (the second must change nothing but the tokens: Projects, Members, Workflows with their ids, Workspaces, Skills), runs the agents but not the personas, and acts itself as ada (admin), kai (files Checkout with Break down and owns it; the agents report to him) and mai (answers the question, moves the help page). It checks each scenario as it happens — the lapse recorded with no actor and the Task waiting at Triage; stuck's Claim at Deploy in `GET /v1/tasks` with its holder and a moving expiry, kai's take-back and stuck's exit 3; the Breakdown's six Subtasks and Checkout a Parent at no Step, which kai cannot complete (`tasks_open`); the prober offered nothing until mai moves the help page to Docs and then exactly it; a watcher never seeing a holder on a Task at Backlog; the question filed beside the screen under Checkout, blocking it, which mai alone can take; both builds advanced along `pass` to Review and into Done by the reviewer; QA claimed only after both builds ended; the Parent completed once kai drops the Backlog leftovers, filing its Retrospective; `build-acme` v2 published by the reviewer — and then, with the bots stopped, that every Task is at exactly one Step or none (an open Task that is neither a Parent nor aimed at a Member at one Step of its Project's Workflow, any other at none), a replay of the whole Activity putting each Task at the Step it is at (filed, moved, advanced, completed, dropped, became a Parent, each `from` the Step it was at, and no claim at a hold), and the order of the trail (gapless, each Claim ended once before the next, the only moves by hand the planner's and mai's, the question filed and blocking in one write inside the builder's one Claim, the Retrospective filed in the Parent's completing write, the version published in the review's). It takes about 15 s on either engine.

### The accounting preset

One Project, `TAX` Tax, worked by people alone: no agent and no Workspace. Skills, written as the practice's procedures: `client-comms`, `bookkeeping`, `partner-review`. `bot.AccountingWorkflow`:

| Step | Skill | Outcomes |
|---|---|---|
| Backlog | — (a hold) | — (the partner moves a Task on) |
| Gather | client-comms | `gathered` → Prepare |
| Prepare | bookkeeping | `prepared` → Partner review |
| Partner review | partner-review | `lodged` → Done · `needs changes` → Prepare |

Lodging is the outcome into Done rather than a Step of its own: a Member who held a Task under one Skill takes it again only under that Skill, so the partner who reviews it lodges it in the same Claim, and each Step is a different person's. Templates: "Q1 BAS — Northwind Traders", filed alone into Backlog, whose gathering asks the partner "Statements for March are missing — ask Northwind?"; "FY26 accounts — Contoso Pty Ltd", a Parent with the Subtasks "Financial statements" (filed into Backlog; the partner sends them back once: "Depreciation on the van is missing from the profit and loss; add it and send it back.") and "Company tax return" (blocked by the statements, filed into Backlog and moved to Gather once its blocker is set); and "Fix the GST code on invoice 1042", filed alone straight at Prepare. Every Task has a description, and each Item a workpaper line per Step, which the worker attaches as Evidence and the advance's Note repeats.

| Who | Skills | What it does | What it proves |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lan Pham (persona) | client-comms | Takes the Tasks at Gather from her takeable list, notes, attaches the workpaper, asks the partner what only the client can answer (holding the Task until he answers), and advances along `gathered`. | A person working a Step; a question aimed at a person. |
| Mai Tran (persona) | bookkeeping | Prepares at Prepare and advances along `prepared`; a Task sent back she reworks, appending the fix as her Note. | The rework after `needs changes`. |
| Kai Nguyen (persona, partner) | partner-review | Owns the work. Answers the questions aimed at him (Claim, Note, Complete); reviews at Partner review, sending the statements back along `needs changes` the first time and lodging along `lodged` otherwise; every round completes the Parents whose Subtasks have all ended and moves one unblocked Task out of Backlog to the Step its Item names. | The hold never offered until moved; the Owner's Complete; no Retrospective where the Workflow has no retro Step. |

`TestBotsAccounting` runs on a fresh Install (`init --no-agents`): Setup twice, then the checks that TAX's Workflow is the accounting one, Connectors and all, and that the Organisation has no agent and no Workspace. The admin files the three templates for Kai; Kai is held back until the BAS and the statements have sat in Backlog untaken and not takeable by Lan, while Mai prepares the GST fix and it waits at Partner review; then each is taken by Lan only after Kai's move. It checks that Lan's question is aimed at Kai, blocks the BAS in the same write inside Lan's Claim and stands alone (the BAS has no Parent), is claimed by Kai alone and answered before the BAS leaves Gather; that the BAS was held by Lan, Mai and Kai in turn, and the statements by Lan, Mai, Kai, Mai and Kai, advancing along `gathered`, `prepared`, `needs changes`, `prepared` and then `lodged`, with the hand-back and the fix among their Notes; that no Task was held by one person under two Skills; that the tax return was claimed only after the statements were lodged; that Kai completed the Parent after both, and that no Retrospective was filed; that a watcher never saw a holder at Backlog; and, with the bots stopped and their tokens revoked, every Task at exactly one Step or none, a replay of the Activity agreeing, and every Note one sentence. It takes about 12 s on SQLite and 15 s on Postgres.

### The live load

`go run ./tools/bots` takes an admin's token and a preset, makes what the preset needs when it is missing (Projects with an empty Workflow, then the preset's Workflow, written only when it differs, Steps kept by name with their ids; Skills; Workspaces with their repositories; the agents reporting to the manager persona; the personas in their Projects with their Skills; the admin in every Project; names are kept, a deactivated Member is reactivated), issues each bot and persona a fresh token named `tools/bots <time>`, files the preset's Tasks in turn, owned by the owning persona, when fewer than `--tasks` have work left outside the hold (and, for software, keeps the chores open at Triage and Deploy in `OPS` for the lapser and stuck), builds `./cmd/darkory` when the preset has stuck, and prints every step as it happens, starting with the preset. When it stops — after `--for` (10 minutes by default; `0` runs until Ctrl-C) or on Ctrl-C — it revokes the tokens it issued, which ends any Claim a bot or persona still holds.

Against `make dev`'s Install (the server on 7358; use 7357 with `make serve`), from the repository root of the checkout `make dev` runs in, in a second terminal:

```sh
DARKORY_TOKEN=$(grep -o 'dk_[A-Za-z0-9_-]*' .dev/init.txt | head -1) \
  go run ./tools/bots --url http://127.0.0.1:7358 --preset accounting --pace human --for 10m
```

```
14:02:00.112 preset accounting on http://127.0.0.1:7358 as tuongaz: no agents in TAX, reporting to Kai Nguyen, asking Kai Nguyen; Lan Pham and Mai Tran and Kai Nguyen; Tasks owned by Kai Nguyen; pace human, for 10m0s
14:02:00.118 owner filed TAX-1 "Q1 BAS — Northwind Traders" for Kai Nguyen
14:02:00.131 owner filed TAX-2 "FY26 accounts — Contoso Pty Ltd" for Kai Nguyen, with 2 Subtasks
14:02:31.004 Kai Nguyen moved        TAX-1 "Q1 BAS — Northwind Traders" to Gather, out of Backlog
14:03:12.502 Lan Pham   asked        TAX-1 TAX-6 aimed at Kai Nguyen: "Statements for March are missing — ask Northwind?"; TAX-1 is blocked until it ends
14:03:51.870 Kai Nguyen noted        TAX-6 "Northwind sent the March statements this morning; they are in the folder now."
14:04:30.250 Lan Pham   advanced     TAX-1 along "gathered", now at Prepare, with the Note "Received the January to March statements for the cheque and card accounts."
14:07:47.553 Kai Nguyen advanced     TAX-3 along "needs changes", now at Prepare, with the Note "Depreciation on the van is missing from the profit and loss; add it and send it back."
14:09:49.308 Kai Nguyen completed    TAX-3 advancing along "lodged", with the Note "Signed off the financial statements with a net profit of $214,660."
```

At the human pace a worker spends 30–90 s on a Task and heartbeats every 15 s (Claims time out after 45 s), a persona answers or takes their work 20–60 s after a Task becomes theirs, the owning persona looks over their Tasks every 30 s, the lapser lapses once a minute, stuck holds its Task until someone takes it back and takes it again two minutes later, and a worker waits three minutes for an answer before releasing its Task. What a person can do while it runs: answer a question from the Inbox, with `--humans=false` (it is then aimed at the admin, or at `--ask`); drag a Task out of Backlog on the board and watch it taken; take back stuck's "Deploy to staging"; watch a Task sent back along "needs changes" and reworked; complete a Parent, after which retro proposes the company Skill's next version and the reviewer publishes it. `--humans=false` runs without personas: the admin owns the Tasks, the questions are aimed at the admin, and `--complete` completes the admin's Parents as their Subtasks end, dropping what waited in the hold a round after the rest ended. `--pace fast` runs everything at the tests' pace. Never point it at an Install whose record matters: it files Tasks under the admin's name and sets the preset's Workflow on its Projects. Both presets can run on one Install one after the other, but not at once.

| Flag | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `--url` | `DARKORY_URL`, else `http://127.0.0.1:7357` | the Install |
| `--token` | `DARKORY_TOKEN` | an admin's token (the variable keeps it out of `ps`) |
| `--preset` | `software` | `software` or `accounting` |
| `--humans` | on | run the preset's personas, each with its own token: they answer the questions, own the Tasks and complete them; off, the admin is asked and owns the Tasks |
| `--workspace-root` | `bots` in `DARKORY_DATA`, else `.dev/bots` | where a preset's Workspaces get their repositories, `<root>/<name>`; a Workspace that exists keeps its path |
| `--pace` | `human` | `human` or `fast` |
| `--for` | `10m` | how long the bots work; `0` until interrupted |
| `--project`, `--project-name` | the preset's first (`WEB` Web; `TAX` Tax) | the key of the Project whose Tasks the bots work, and its name if it must be created |
| `--ops`, `--ops-name` | `OPS` Ops | the key of the software preset's second Project, whose chores the lapser and stuck take, and its name if it must be created |
| `--ask` | the answering persona with `--humans`, else the admin | who the agents' questions are aimed at, unless an Item names someone |
| `--tasks` | `3` | Tasks with work left to keep filed |
| `--complete` | off | complete, as the admin, the Parents it filed and owns once their Subtasks have ended (the owning persona does this with `--humans`) |
| `--darkory` | built from `./cmd/darkory` | the binary stuck runs |
| `--insecure` | off | let stuck's CLI use plain `http://` to another host |

## Runner

The Runner (`internal/runner`, [ADR 0013](../adr/0013-a-runner-starts-agent-sessions.md)) pulls Tasks through `next` as each agent Member it has a token for, prepares a git worktree per Workspace the Task names under `<data>/workspaces/<KEY>/`, writes `<data>/sessions/<KEY>/prompt.md` and `mcp.json`, starts the agent's command — in tmux when the machine has it, as a child process otherwise, logging to `pane.log` — sends Heartbeats while the session's progress file moves, nudges an agent that stops without a decision, ends the session when the Claim ends and attaches the log as Evidence. It merges a Subtask's branch into its Parent's branch when it advances into Done, a Task standing alone into the default branch, and a Parent's branch into the default branch when the Parent completes ([ADR 0014](../adr/0014-feature-branches-and-shipping.md)). Model v2: the Runner still names a Parent's branch `feature/<KEY>`; M3 makes it `<KEY>` and reworks the prompt and Acceptance sessions.

```sh
darkory serve --data .dev                 # runs the Runner too when .dev/agents holds <member>.token files (--runner=auto)
darkory serve --data .dev --runner=off    # the server alone; then, in another terminal:
DARKORY_URL=http://127.0.0.1:7357 darkory runner --data .dev [--member builder]…
darkory sessions                          # what the Runner runs now ("No Runner is attached" when serve has none)
darkory join WEB-12 [--readonly] [--data .dev]     # join the session's tmux pane; detach with the prefix and d
darkory sessions nudge WEB-12 | darkory sessions stop WEB-12   # admins
```

The sessions run on a tmux server of the Runner's own, `tmux -L darkory-<8 hex of the data directory's path>`, so `tmux ls` does not show them; `darkory join` finds it from `--data`. `DARKORY_RUNNER_TMUX=off` (or `darkory runner --tmux off`) runs them as child processes, which cannot be joined. That server reads no tmux configuration (`-f /dev/null`): no status bar, 10000 lines of scrollback, `TERM=screen-256color`, none of the person's key tables or plugins.

**What a session runs with.** Its environment is the Runner's making, not the server's: `PATH` (the Runner's darkory first), `HOME`, `USER`, `LOGNAME`, `SHELL`, `LANG`, `LC_*`, `TERM`, `TMPDIR`, `TZ`, `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`, the proxy variables, `ANTHROPIC_*`, `DARKORY_NO_UPDATE_CHECK` and, when set, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and `CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR` from the server's, plus whatever the server's `DARKORY_RUNNER_ENV` names (comma-separated: where the secrets an agent needs go, since agent settings are every Member's to read), then `DARKORY_URL`, `DARKORY_TOKEN`, `DARKORY_SESSION` and the agent's `env`. A `serve` started inside Claude Code or a tmux session therefore hands its sessions no `CLAUDECODE`, `CLAUDE_CODE_*`, `TMUX` or `TMUX_PANE`. Claude Code runs with **the person's own Claude Code configuration**: `~/.claude` and `~/.claude.json` (or their `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`), their sign-in from the Keychain or `~/.claude/.credentials.json`, their trust decisions, and **their hooks, plugins, status line, `CLAUDE.md`, skills, agents, commands, MCP servers and permission rules, by their choice**: a status line can print their account and usage into the session's log, which is Evidence the Organisation reads, and a hook can start Claude sessions of its own (the check by hand in agents-plan.md's "Smoke run" saw a plugin's review session start on the builder's commit). The Runner writes none of it. A Workspace the person has opened in Claude Code is trusted already, and Claude Code keys the trust on the repository, so each Task's worktree is too; their `skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt`, set once they accepted Bypass Permissions mode, covers `--dangerously-skip-permissions`. Transcripts go to `~/.claude/projects/<the worktree's slug>/`.

A repository never opened in Claude Code makes it ask on a terminal, before any model turn, "Quick safety check: Is this a project you created or one you trust?" and, for a person who never accepted it, the Bypass Permissions mode warning. The Runner answers these only as a fallback, and narrowly, since anything the agent prints could imitate a dialog: in a Claude Code session in tmux, before the agent's model has answered at all (its transcript absent or with no assistant message), one dialog per session, and only when the visible screen is exactly that dialog of Claude Code 2.1.289 (the session's own folder in it, nothing under its "Enter to confirm · Esc to cancel"): Down and Enter, the only keys it ever presses into a session, and a Note "The runner accepted Claude Code's first-run prompt: …". Claude Code saves the answer in the person's own files, as if they had given it. A dialog it may not answer (after the first turn, or a second in the session, such as the bypass warning after the trust dialog for a person who never accepted it) gets no key: the session shows `waiting` and a Note says a person can answer it with `darkory join <KEY>`; unanswered, the Claim lapses on the usual rule.

The session's log, attached as Evidence when it ends, is the pane's output as the agent's terminal received it (`tmux pipe-pane`), nothing added or redacted, the person's status line included when they have one.

`tools/fakeagent` stands in for Claude Code: set an agent's command to it (`darkory agent set builder --command <path>/fakeagent --arg=--prompt-file --arg={prompt_file} --arg=--progress --arg=/tmp/p/{session_id}.jsonl --arg=--mcp-config --arg={mcp_config} --progress-file /tmp/p/{session_id}.jsonl --env FAKEAGENT_SCENARIO=advance`). It reads the prompt, writes its progress as a transcript, notes, commits in the first Workspace, attaches a test log, then per `FAKEAGENT_SCENARIO`: `advance` (default: along `FAKEAGENT_OUTCOME`, or the Step's one way out; a Breakdown first files the Subtasks `FAKEAGENT_BREAKDOWN` lists, `step:title;…` with the step left empty for the Project's first work Step, naming `FAKEAGENT_WORKSPACES`), `complete`, `question`, `silent`, `hang`, `busy` or `crash`. `FAKEAGENT_FILE` names the file it commits, so two Tasks can conflict. `FAKEAGENT_PROMPT` makes it draw Claude Code 2.1.289's folder-trust dialog and Bypass Permissions mode warning first and wait for Down, Enter: `claude` (as Claude Code does, unless the person's `~/.claude.json` or `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` trusts the folder or its repository and their settings accepted the skip), `trust`, or `again` (the trust dialog twice); `late` draws the trust dialog after its first turn instead, saying "the dialog was answered" should a Down reach it; the Runner treats it as Claude Code when it is started through a script named `claude`.

`DARKORY_RUNNER_TIMINGS` shortens the Runner's clocks for tests, as `name=duration` pairs: `wait` (next's wait, 30s), `timeout` (the Claims' heartbeat timeout, 5m), `tick` (progress read and Heartbeat, 30s), `stale` (no Heartbeat after, 2m), `nudge` (between nudges and before the release, 2m), `exit` (after /exit, 30s), `poll` (merged pull requests, 1m), `retry` (after a failure, 5s). The e2e tests use `wait=1s,timeout=10s,tick=200ms,stale=2s,nudge=700ms,exit=3s,poll=1s,retry=300ms`.

What the tests hold:

- `internal/runner` unit tests: the command template (placeholders, Claude Code's defaults and first message, the permission skip, a misspelt placeholder), shell quoting through a real `sh`; the transcript's project slug and real path, the turn-ended reading of Claude Code 2.1's records and of `TURN_ENDED`, a transcript longer than the tail read; the prompt (golden files in `testdata/`, `go test ./internal/runner -run TestBuildPrompt -update` rewrites them), escapes and quoted record text included; the checkout planner; `Prepare` against real git (the Break down making `feature/<KEY>`, a later session reusing the worktree or the branch, removal keeping the branch and a dirty worktree, a person's branch refused, a quick Feature from main); every merge path (merge-tree into a branch checked out nowhere, two parents, nothing touched; again is a no-op; a conflict moves nothing; into the checked-out main, clean, and its conflict aborted; uncommitted changes refusing it); the child and tmux hosts (environment from a 0600 file, typed lines, the pane's log, exit status, kill); the pane tail with escapes taken out. After the smoke run: a session's environment (`TestBaseEnv`, `DARKORY_RUNNER_ENV`; `TestChildHostEnvironment`, `TestTmuxHostEnvironment` on a tmux server started with `CLAUDECODE` in its own environment); the tmux server reading no configuration from a `HOME` whose `.tmux.conf` sets options (`TestTmuxHostReadsNoConfiguration`); and the first-run dialogs found exactly on the smoke's capture and a fresh directory's, and not for another folder, with Claude Code's prompt under them, with the choice moved, in the older wording or as words in a line (`TestFindFirstRunPrompt`); a transcript's first assistant message (`TestHasAssistantMessage`).
- `internal/runner` in-process tests (`runner_test.go`): the fixture (Project WEB with a git Workspace as its default, agents on the fake agent) stays; model v2: the scenarios that went with Features — `TestRunnerWorksAFeature`, `TestRunnerMergesATaskCompletedWithoutReview`, `TestRunnerStartsTheNextSessionOnceTheEarlierEnds`, `TestRunnerSessionStates`, `TestRunnerReleasesASilentSession`, `TestRunnerInTmux`, `TestRunnerTerminal`, `TestRunnerPullRequestMode` and the three `claude_test.go` scenarios — come back in M3 on Parents and Steps; `e2e/runner_test.go` covers the Runner end to end meanwhile.
- `internal/mcp` `TestNoHeartbeatsLeavesTheClaimToTheRunner`; `cmd/darkory` `TestJoinNeedsASession`, `TestRunnerNeedsTokens`; `internal/config` the `--runner` setting.
- `e2e/runner_test.go` (`make e2e`, `make e2e-pg`): darkory init's roster in a fresh repository on the default Workflow, every agent on the fake agent (the planner and builder advance along their Step's one way, the reviewer `pass`, retro `done`), serve's Runner with the timings above: `TestRunnerWorksAParent` (scenarios 2, 3, 4, 11: a Task filed with Break down, two Subtasks naming two Workspaces, two builders, merges in both repositories noted on the Subtasks, the Owner's Complete merging the Parent's branch into main), `TestRunnerEndsSessionsWithoutADecision` (5, 6 with the hung session `stalled` through `/v1`, 7), `TestRunnerStandaloneAndAutoComplete` (4: a Task standing alone merged into main; a Parent with Auto-complete completing itself and merging), `TestRunnerMergesATaskCompletedWithoutReview` (a Workflow whose Build leads into Done: the builder completes, merged into main, noted as without review), `TestRunnerMergeConflict` (9: the resolving Subtask at Build), `TestRunnerAlone` (12: `darkory runner` beside `serve --runner=off`), `TestRunnerInTmux` (skipped without tmux: `dk-MAIN-1` on the Runner's tmux server, stopped by an admin through `/v1`). The harness starts every other test's server with `--runner=off`.

## The Postgres the tests need

Postgres 14 or newer, and a role that may create databases. The URL names any database the role can connect to (`postgres` is fine); tests never write to it. Each test creates its own database, `dk_test_<random>`, from `template0`, and drops it `WITH (FORCE)` when the test ends, so packages can run in parallel against one server.

A throwaway local server on the port the Makefile expects:

```sh
initdb -D /tmp/dk-pg -U dk --auth=trust
pg_ctl -D /tmp/dk-pg -o "-p 54329" -l /tmp/dk-pg.log start
```

or with Docker:

```sh
docker run -d --name dk-pg -p 54329:5432 -e POSTGRES_USER=dk -e POSTGRES_HOST_AUTH_METHOD=trust postgres:14
```

If a test run is killed before its cleanup, drop what it left behind:

```sh
psql "$DARKORY_TEST_POSTGRES_URL" -Atc "SELECT 'DROP DATABASE \"' || datname || '\" WITH (FORCE);' FROM pg_database WHERE datname LIKE 'dk_test_%'" | psql "$DARKORY_TEST_POSTGRES_URL"
```

## Writing a test that runs on both

Use `internal/store/storetest`. `Each` runs the body once per engine as subtests named `sqlite` and `postgres`, each with a fresh, migrated database:

```go
func TestSomething(t *testing.T) {
	storetest.Each(t, func(t *testing.T, s *store.Store) {
		org := storetest.Organisation(t, s)
		err := s.Write(t.Context(), org, func(tx store.Tx, seq int64) error {
			// …
		})
		// …
	})
}
```

- `storetest.Open(t, engine)` and `storetest.OpenUnmigrated(t, engine)` give one database on a named engine.
- `storetest.DSN(t, engine)` gives an empty database's DSN, for tests that open several Stores on one database.
- A Postgres-only test asks for `store.Postgres` directly; it skips when the URL is unset.

Write queries once, with `$1, $2…` placeholders; both drivers accept them, repeated and in any order.

## What guards what

- **Model v2 (M1b), current:** `internal/server` `projects_test.go` (Projects, Workflows with live facts, moves, Step listing, Rank and ownership through the client) and `mvp_test.go` (the MVP flow on Steps, refusals carrying `details.outcomes`, kept and replayed under an Idempotency-Key); `internal/cli` `TestPhase2Flow` (Break down, Subtasks, a question beside its Task, `advance` and its refusals, take-back, Rank, ownership, the Owner's Complete, a Retrospective's proposal published by `advance publish`), `TestWorkflowCommands` (`workflow show --body` edited and set, filing into a hold, `move`, Labels) and `TestCommandsFormTheirRequests`; `internal/mcp` `TestAdvanceMoveAndSplit` and the tools of `TestToolsAndRules`; `e2e/` as below, with the soak's invariant that a Task is at exactly one Step of its own Project or none. The entries after this one record what each earlier phase added, in the words of its time; where a test they name went with Features, Teams or Statuses, its v2 successor is named here.
- **Activity about a Task (M3):** `internal/core` `TestActivityAboutATask` (a Parent's entries with its Subtasks', by key or id; a Subtask's its own; a blocker added to another Task not about the one it names; composed with `kind`, `member` and `project`, paged backwards; an unknown Task `not_found`), `internal/server` `TestActivityAboutATaskThroughTheClient`, the `activity --task` row of `TestPhase2CommandsFormTheirRequests`; in the web app, `Activity.test.tsx` (the Task filter sent to /v1, a Subtask's stream entry joining its Parent's) and `task.test.tsx` (a Task's path is one read with `task`).
- **`init` always seeds Project MAIN (M3):** `internal/core` `TestInitSeedsProjectMainWithoutTheRoster` (`InitOptions{Project: true}`: MAIN on the default Workflow holding the first Member alone, no agents, no Workspace) on both engines; `cmd/darkory` `TestInitOutsideAGitRepository` (`--no-agents` prints Project MAIN and makes no agents, token files or Workspace) and `TestInitSeedsTheRosterInAGitRepository` (`--no-agents` inside a repository adds no Workspace).
- `internal/store`: `Write` numbers Activity without gaps in commit order under 50 concurrent writers, with no "database is locked" on SQLite; the migration runner, its SQLite backup and its refusal of a newer database; `TestSchemaIsTheSameOnBothEngines` compares tables, columns, nullability, primary keys, indexes and foreign keys after migrating each engine (it skips without Postgres, having nothing to compare with); `TestEveryTableCarriesOrgID`.
- `internal/server/gen`: `TestSpecKeepsTheConventions` validates `api/openapi.yaml` and checks every operation for `Idempotency-Key` on writes, the credential requirement, and the `Error` default response.
- `internal/store` also: `WriteBatch` takes the counter first and a failed guard rolls everything back; `TestWriteBatchIsOneRoundTripOnPostgres` counts the round trips on the wire (`storetest.Wire`).
- `internal/core`, on both engines with a fake clock (`clock.Fake`): every branch of the Takeable rule and its negative (`rule_test.go`); lapses at expiry, a late Heartbeat refused, the lapse recorded once by whoever meets it first, Session binding, revocation and close ending Claims, idempotent claims (`claim_test.go`); admin operations, the admin mark, Reporting-line cycles, filing (`admin_test.go`). The race suite (`race_test.go`): 50 claims of one Task give one winner and 49 `already_claimed`; 20 `next` callers over 10 Tasks claim each once and leave nothing takeable; a late Heartbeat racing a claimer and the sweeper records one lapse; a reader following `after` under concurrent writers sees every Activity number in order; concurrent retries under one Idempotency-Key make one write. `TestHotPathWritesAreOneRoundTripOnPostgres` checks claim, `next`'s claim, heartbeat, release and complete each send one batch in one round trip. Run the race suite repeatedly with `go test -race -count=5 -run Race ./internal/core/`.
- `internal/core`, Phase 2: Handover and no self-review, the holder's Notes and Observations, take-back up the Reporting line, the owner's Task drop (`flow_test.go`); Blocking across Features, cycles, the authority to block, questions and Escalations (`blocking_test.go`); Rank, ship, drop and its cascade, ownership, the owner's fallback for the Break down and the Retrospective, a Retrospective sorting by its ended Feature's Rank (`features_test.go`); proposals, publishing, the stale base, the author's refusal, Observations reviewed, a Feature filed from a Retrospective (`retro_test.go`); every Activity kind written is listed (`kinds_test.go`). Races: two opposite block edges and a triangle never both close (`TestRaceOppositeBlockEdges`, run it with `-count=20`); ship against filing a Task (`TestRaceShipAgainstFilingATask`). The round-trip test also covers handover, note, observe and a publishing complete.
- `internal/blob`: the disk store's put, get and delete; keys that would leave the store are refused; a short, long or cancelled put leaves no file.
- `internal/server`: health with its sign-in modes, JSON 404s under `/v1`, and the web app at `/`; through the generated Go client on both engines: no credential is 401 even from 127.0.0.1, a token without a Session is `session_required`, the claim path from filing a Feature to completing its Break down, idempotency keys, a login link signing a browser in, the Activity stream resuming with `Last-Event-ID`, and its first bytes (`: connected`) arriving at once, before any event or keep-alive. `security_test.go`: a cookie write from another origin, a sibling port or with no Origin or Referer is 403 while one from the Install's own origin passes and bearer writes need no Origin; JSON bodies need `application/json`; the Activity stream ends without sending more once its token is revoked or its Session closed. `flow_test.go`: health's sign-in modes and update notice; Activity read backwards and the stream from now; the Activity enums match the core; Evidence on both engines (the holder and Team rules, the size limit, path filenames, retries, nosniff attachments). `mvp_test.go`: the MVP flow through the generated client on both engines, from a human filing a Feature to a published Skill version and a later Claim under it. In `internal/core`, `TestRevocationStopsLongRequestsAndClaims` covers a waiting `next` and a claim from an ended Session.
